note: Superset of updated_tools_defs_v3.json (the OpenAI function-calling format actually sent to the model). category/action_type/confirmation/call_before/related_tools/notes are structured fields derived from updated_tools_defs_v3.json's prose. output_schema is sourced from tools.json's hand-authored inputs/outputs/prerequisites spec (the authoritative reference-shape documentation for engineering and eval use) and converted to JSON-Schema shape; it is not sent to the model. Tools absent from tools.json (currently: get_all_requests) keep a hand-authored output_schema instead, since tools.json has not been updated with this tool yet.

global_conventions.auth: Handled entirely by the platform. All tools execute inside an already-authenticated customer session; no auth token is passed between tools. Every write tool still requires explicit customer confirmation in conversation before it is called.
global_conventions.session_context: login_context (customer_id, full_name, date_of_birth, gender, customer_since, customer_segment, registered_mobile, registered_email, communication_address, permanent_address, kyc_status, pan_masked, preferred_language, linked_products_summary, linked_accounts, linked_products, linked_cards) is injected into the system prompt at session start. linked_products entries carry their product type (fd, rd, loan, policy). linked_products_summary is a quick-glance count by type only — full IDs still come from linked_products. date_of_birth and customer_segment (enum: regular | premium | wealth | senior_citizen | staff) are the eligibility signals for senior_citizen_rate in get_deposit_loan_rates and for personalised offers in get_products_and_offers. kyc_status (enum: verified | pending | expired) may cause write tools to fail — check the returned message field in that case. communication_address/permanent_address reflect the last verified update, not any pending address-update request submitted via raise_request. registered_mobile, registered_email, and pan_masked are masked, display-only values. All IDs passed to tools must come from login_context or from a prior tool result — never invented or assumed.
global_conventions.naming: Array inputs use plural names (e.g. account_ids). All IDs are opaque tokens, never raw PANs or card numbers.
global_conventions.write_outcomes: Every write tool returns status (success|failed) and message (human-readable outcome or failure reason). Tools that act directly on an account, card or deposit also return reference_id (audit reference). Tools that create a trackable service request — raise_request, request_cheque_book, request_duplicate_statement — return request_id instead; that IS their audit reference, and they do not return reference_id.
global_conventions.dates: YYYY-MM-DD for dates, ISO 8601 for timestamps.
global_conventions.amounts: Always positive numbers. Direction (credit/debit) is carried by a separate 'type' field, never by the sign of the amount. All amounts are in INR (Indian Rupees) unless otherwise stated.
global_conventions.confirmation_policy: action_type='write' tools require explicit customer confirmation in the conversation before being called, regardless of whether prerequisites were already satisfied.

tools.name: search_knowledge_base
tools.summary: Searches the bank's knowledge corpus (product documents, RBI circulars, scheme details, FAQs, how-to guides) with a natural-language query. Use for policy, process, eligibility, or regulatory questions that cannot be answered from the customer's own account or product data.
notes: Any rule or policy quoted in a response to the customer must be grounded in the snippets returned by this tool — never asserted from memory.

query.description: Natural-language question or search phrase. Example: 'premature FD penalty rules'.

chunk.description: retrieved text; quote or paraphrase this when grounding a policy answer.

source.description: title, circular number, or URL identifying the source document.

results.description: Ranked list of retrieved text chunks, most relevant first.

tools.name: get_account_balance
tools.summary: Returns current available balance and hold/lien amount for one or more linked accounts.

available_balance.description: spendable balance = total balance minus hold_amount.

hold_amount.description: amount under lien/hold, excluded from available_balance

tools.name: get_account_details
tools.summary: Returns account metadata — type, status, home branch, IFSC, holders, nominee, open date. Does not return balances (use get_account_balance) or transactions (use get_transaction_history).

tools.name: get_transaction_history
tools.summary: Returns statement entries for a single account, newest first, with date/direction/channel filters and pagination.
notes: Each returned entry includes a status field (e.g. success, pending, failed, reversed) reflecting the transaction's processing state. This status is specific to this tool's output — it is not carried into the official statement produced by request_duplicate_statement.

from_date.description: Start of date range. No lower bound if omitted.

to_date.description: End of date range. No upper bound if omitted.

reference_id.description: UTR/RRN/internal ID; pass as related_transaction_id in raise_request for disputes

transaction_note.description: narration or payee/reference detail as received from the payment rail, e.g. payee name, UPI handle, or biller reference.

status.description: the transaction's processing state; specific to this tool's output and not carried into the official statement produced by request_duplicate_statement.

total_count.description: Total matching rows across all pages, not just this page.

tools.name: get_fd_details
tools.summary: Returns full details of the customer's Fixed Deposits.
notes: Mandatory prerequisite before update_deposit_renewal and get_deposit_closure_quote — always surface the current state before proposing a change or showing a closure quote.

payout_account defaults to source_account at the time of booking and cannot be changed on an active deposit. The only way to redirect proceeds is the optional payout_account override at close_deposit time.

tools.name: get_rd_details
tools.summary: Returns full details of the customer's Recurring Deposits, including installment amount, installments paid so far, and total accumulated to date.
notes: Mandatory prerequisite before update_deposit_renewal and get_deposit_closure_quote — always surface the current state before proposing a change or showing a closure quote.
total_deposited is the accumulated-so-far figure; maturity_amount is the projected final figure. Do not conflate the two when answering the customer.

payout_account defaults to source_account at the time of booking and cannot be changed on an active deposit. The only way to redirect proceeds is the optional payout_account override at close_deposit time.

installments_paid.description: number of installments paid so far

tools.name: get_deposit_loan_rates
tools.summary: Returns the current rate card for a deposit or loan product, by tenure/amount slab. The sole authoritative source for any rate used in a calculator or a booking — never use memory, assumption, or a customer-supplied rate.

tenure_months.description: Filter to the slab covering this tenure. All slabs if omitted.

amount.description: Filter to the slab covering this amount. All slabs if omitted.

senior_citizen_rate.description: present only when product_type is fd or rd; absent for all loan product types.

effective_date.description: Date this rate card became effective.

tools.name: calculate_fd_maturity
tools.summary: Computes maturity value and interest earned for a Fixed Deposit. Compounding is quarterly by default (bank standard) and not configurable via input.

call_before.reason: rate must be sourced here, never assumed or taken from the customer

notes: For payout_type of monthly or quarterly, the maturity_amount returned is principal only — interest is paid out periodically during the tenure rather than accumulated to maturity.

maturity_amount.description: Value at maturity. For monthly/quarterly payout: principal only (interest already paid out during tenure).

tools.name: calculate_rd_maturity
tools.summary: Computes maturity value and interest earned for a Recurring Deposit. Interest is always paid at maturity. Compounding is quarterly by default (bank standard) and not configurable via input.

call_before.reason: rate must be sourced here, never assumed or taken from the customer

notes: Mandatory prerequisite before create_rd.
RDs have no periodic payout option — interest always accrues and is credited only at maturity, unlike FDs which support monthly/quarterly payout.

tenure_months.description: Tenure in months (= number of installments).

maturity_amount.description: Total value at maturity: all installments plus interest.

tools.name: create_fd
tools.summary: Books a new Fixed Deposit, debiting principal_amount from the source account as a one-time transaction.

call_before.reason: obtain the applicable rate based on the user's age
show the customer the rate and projected maturity value before booking
verify the source account can fund principal_amount

notes: payout_account is not a separate input — proceeds to source_account and cannot be changed later on an active deposit.

If payout_type is non-cumulative (monthly or quarterly), maturity_instruction cannot be renew_principal_interest — interest is already being paid out periodically, so there is no accumulated interest left to renew. Only no_renewal or renew_principal are valid in that case.

source_account.description: Linked account to debit once, at booking.

guardian_name.description: Required if nominee's date_of_birth indicates the nominee is under 18 at the time of registration. Must be validated at call time even though not schema-enforced.

principal_amount.description: Echo of the principal amount debited at booking.

nominee.description: Registered nominee {name, relationship}. Absent if none.

tools.name: create_rd
tools.summary: Books a new Recurring Deposit. This authorizes a recurring monthly debit of monthly_installment from source_account for the entire tenure; the first installment is debited at booking. This recurring commitment must be stated explicitly when seeking customer confirmation.

call_before.reason: show the customer the rate and projected maturity value before booking
verify the source account can fund the first installment — note this does NOT verify the customer can sustain the full multi-month commitment; confirm that separately in conversation

notes: payout_account is not a separate input — proceeds default to source_account and cannot be changed later on an active deposit.
No payout_type input — RDs always pay interest at maturity only.

maturity_instruction is optional and defaults to no_renewal. It can only be set here, at booking: update_deposit_renewal is FD-only, so an RD's maturity instruction cannot be changed once the RD is active.

tenure_months.description: Tenure in months (= number of installments).

source_account.description: Linked account debited monthly for the full tenure.

guardian_name.description: Required if nominee's date_of_birth indicates the nominee is under 18 at the time of registration. Must be validated at call time even though not schema-enforced.

monthly_debit_date.description: Day of month subsequent installments will be debited.

nominee.description: Registered nominee {name, relationship}. Absent if none.

tools.name: get_deposit_closure_quote
tools.summary: Quotes the payout if an FD or RD were closed today. Before maturity, interest is credited only at the card rate applicable to the period the deposit has actually run — normally lower than the rate contracted for its original tenure — and a separate premature-closure charge of penalty_rate% of principal_amount is then deducted. After maturity no charge applies (penalty_rate = 0) and the full contracted interest is paid. estimated_payout is the net figure after any charge; effective_rate is the net annual rate the customer actually earns. Read-only — does not close anything.

call_before.reason: surface the current FD state before showing the closure quote
surface the current RD state before showing the closure quote

notes: Mandatory prerequisite before close_deposit — the quote, including any penalty, must be shown to the customer before they confirm closure.
When penalty_rate is 0 (post-maturity closure), penalty_amount will also be 0.
principal_amount (number) is returned for both FD and RD quotes: for an FD it is the original principal (see get_fd_details.principal_amount); for an RD it is the sum of installments paid to date.

principal_amount.description: in case of FD it is the original principal (see get_fd_details.principal_amount), in case of RD it is sum of installments paid to date.

accrued_interest.description: interest accrued to date at the card rate applicable to the period the deposit has actually run, BEFORE the premature-closure charge is deducted

penalty_rate.description: premature-closure charge as a percentage of principal_amount; 0 if the deposit has already matured

penalty_amount.description: the charge itself: principal_amount x penalty_rate / 100

effective_rate.description: net annual rate (%) the customer actually earns, i.e. after the premature-closure charge

estimated_payout.description: net amount payable on closure today

tools.name: close_deposit
tools.summary: Closes an FD or RD prematurely and credits proceeds to the payout account. For an RD, closure also permanently stops all future monthly installment debits — there is no separate way to 'pause' or 'stop' an RD without closing it.

call_before.reason: show the customer the payout amount and any penalty before they confirm closure

amount_credited.description: Net amount credited after any penalty.

payout_account.description: Account the proceeds were credited to.

tools.name: update_deposit_renewal
tools.summary: Sets the maturity instruction on an active FD. Takes effect on the maturity date, not immediately.

call_before.reason: surface the current instruction and maturity date before changing it

notes: If the deposit's payout_type (from get_fd_details) is non-cumulative (monthly or quarterly), instruction cannot be set to renew_principal_interest — only no_renewal or renew_principal are valid.

tools.name: get_loan_details
tools.summary: Returns current loan state: outstanding balance, EMI, rate, remaining tenure, next due date.

emi_day_of_month.description: day of month EMI falls due (e.g., 5 means the 5th of every month) — not a full date. See next_due_date for the actual upcoming date.

tools.name: get_loan_foreclosure_quote
tools.summary: Quotes the total payoff to close a loan early as of a given date. Informational only — no tool in this system closes a loan.
notes: If a customer asks to 'pause', 'stop', or 'reduce' EMIs, use this tool to show foreclosure cost, since no such capability exists in this system.
No tool in this system closes a loan. After presenting the quote, direct the customer to raise_request or a branch visit to proceed with foreclosure.

as_of_date.description: Value date for the quote. Defaults to the current server date; a future date may be passed to plan ahead.

tools.name: calculate_emi
tools.summary: Computes the fixed monthly EMI, total interest, total repayment, and full amortisation schedule for a loan.

call_before.reason: rate should be sourced here for actual loan bookings; a customer-supplied rate is permitted only for hypothetical/exploratory 'what-if' calculations, not for use in an actual transaction.

notes: Interest and principal split changes every month even though the emi total is fixed — early installments are interest-heavy, later ones principal-heavy, because interest is charged on the shrinking outstanding balance.
closing_balance at the last installment should be 0.

emi.description: The fixed amount payable every month for the full tenure, covering both interest and principal; constant across all installments.

principal_component.description: portion of this installment reducing principal

interest_component.description: portion of this installment paying interest

schedule.description: One entry per installment, up to tenure_months.

tools.name: get_gold_rate
tools.summary: Returns today's gold rate per gram for a given purity. Sole valid source for gold_rate_per_gram in calculate_gold_loan_ltv — never assume, recall, or accept this value from customer input.

purity_karat.description: Must match the purity of the gold being pledged.

rate_per_gram.description: Current rate per gram for this purity.

tools.name: calculate_gold_loan_ltv
tools.summary: Values gold collateral (grams x rate) and applies the bank's current Loan-to-Value cap to compute the maximum eligible loan amount. The LTV cap itself is applied internally by the backend, not supplied by the caller.

call_before.reason: gold_rate_per_gram must come from a fresh call at the same purity — never assumed or customer-supplied

notes: Always pass the rate_per_gram returned by get_gold_rate for the same purity_karat — this links the calculation to a verifiable rate source, which is why the rate must be supplied by the caller rather than fetched internally.

purity_karat.description: Must match the purity used in the get_gold_rate call.

gold_rate_per_gram.description: Rate from get_gold_rate for the same purity.

gold_value.description: Market value of the pledged gold.

eligible_loan_amount.description: Maximum loan at the bank's LTV cap.

ltv_percent_used.description: The LTV cap (%) actually applied, per current bank/RBI policy.

tools.name: get_card_details
tools.summary: Returns card metadata, status, credit/available limits, and per-channel usage controls. Use to diagnose card declines.
notes: Mandatory prerequisite before set_card_controls — surface current settings before proposing changes.

credit_limit.description: present for credit cards only; absent for debit and prepaid card types.

available_limit.description: present for credit cards only; absent for debit and prepaid card types.

controls.description: {atm, online, pos}, each {domestic: {enabled, daily_limit}, international: {enabled, daily_limit}}

tools.name: toggle_card_freeze
tools.summary:
Temporarily freezes or unfreezes a card. Reversible at any time. Use freeze when a card is misplaced but may be found.
For loss, theft, fraud, or damage use block_card instead, which is permanent.
notes: Cannot unfreeze a card whose status is blocked or expired — only active/frozen cards are valid targets.

message.description: Outcome summary / failure reason, e.g. card is blocked and cannot be unfrozen.

tools.name: block_card
tools.summary: Permanently and irreversibly blocks a card. Confirm the customer understands this before calling. For fraud, theft, or loss, block immediately. For damaged cards, block to enable a replacement request. A replacement can be requested via raise_request.
tools.confirmation_note: and also ask for a reason to block the card

tools.name: set_card_controls
tools.summary: Updates per-channel card controls. Each channel (atm, online, pos) has independent domestic and international enable/limit settings. Only provided fields change; omitted fields keep their current values.

call_before.reason: provide current control settings before proposing changes

notes: For enabling/disabling the channel. Only call the tool if the current and requested status is different.

For changing limits, follow: Check if the channel is enabled.; The requested limit must be less than the credit_limit.; The requested limit should not be equal to the current limit; The requested limit should not be negative
For requests containing multiple parameters in a channel/channels: Send the same control dictionary with the requested changes.
Do not make changes to a channel's enable/disable status and daily limit in the same tool call.
If required do sequential tool calls to fulfill the user's request.

The channel objects (atm / online / pos) are optional in the schema but they carry the request: omitting all of them changes nothing. If the customer has not made clear which channel, which region (domestic/international), or what value they want, ask — never guess a channel or invent a limit to avoid asking.

atm.description: ATM cash withdrawal controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

online.description: Online (card-not-present) payment controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

pos.description: In-store POS transaction controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

controls.description: Full resulting controls, all channels and regions, same shape as input.

tools.name: show_mandates
tools.summary: Lists mandates on the customer's profile. Recurring subscription debits are mandates, not card transactions — look them up here, not via card tools.
notes: If a customer asks about a mandate or wants it cancelled, paused or resumed, inform them of this limitation and direct them to raise_request or a branch visit.

account_id.description: Filter to mandates on one linked account. All accounts if omitted.

tools.name: stop_cheque_payment
tools.summary: Places a stop-payment instruction on one or more cheques issued from an account. Only affects cheques that have not already cleared; per-cheque outcomes are returned individually.
notes: Cheque clearing status is checked in the backend at call time, not supplied by the caller — a cheque that has already cleared is returned with a failed per-cheque outcome rather than being blocked pre-emptively by the model.

account_id.description: Linked account the cheques were issued from.

status.description: Overall outcome: success (all stopped) | partial | failed

tools.name: request_cheque_book
tools.summary: Orders a new cheque book for a savings or current account.

delivery_address.description: Address the cheque book will be sent to.

tools.name: request_duplicate_statement
tools.summary: Orders an official duplicate account statement for a date range, delivered by email. Use this — not raw get_transaction_history output
notes: The statement does not include the per-entry status field returned by get_transaction_history — it lists only cleared/posted transactions.

tools.name: raise_request
tools.summary: Registers a complaint or general service request — the single escalation channel for disputes, service issues, and any action no other tool can perform (e.g. card replacement after block_card, insurance premium/claim needs, premature-closure follow-up beyond close_deposit, postal address update).

call_before.reason: locate the disputed transaction and pass its reference_id as related_transaction_id

notes: unauthorized_debit requests are treated as urgent by default.
Never promise a specific outcome, e.g. a fee waiver — the request is routed for review, not resolved on the spot.
related_transaction_id is required when category is failed_transaction or unauthorized_debit — this is not enforced at the schema level and must be validated at call time.
This system has no tool to update a customer's email, phone number, or postal address. Direct customers requesting any of these to raise_request.
category has no default and must always be explicitly chosen — pick the closest fit rather than a catch-all; there is no general_query option.

description.description: What happened / what is needed, with enough context to action it.

related_transaction_id.description: reference_id of the disputed transaction from get_transaction_history. Required for failed_transaction and unauthorized_debit.

account_id.description: Related linked account, if applicable — helps routing.

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.summary: Returns the current status of a previously raised service request. Use when a customer follows up on an earlier request, before raising a duplicate.

request_id.description: Service request ID returned by any request tool.

status.description: enum: open | in_progress | resolved | rejected | cancelled

last_update.description: Most recent activity on the request.

remarks.description: Latest agent/system remarks. Absent if none.

tools.name: get_all_requests
tools.summary: Lists the customer's service requests (raised via raise_request, request_cheque_book, request_duplicate_statement, or stop_cheque_payment), most recent first. Use when a customer asks about their outstanding or past requests generally, without a specific request_id — use get_request_status instead once a specific request_id is known.

category.description: Filter by request category. All categories if omitted.

tools.name: get_insurance_details
tools.summary: Returns policy details for the customer's bancassurance policies. No premium-payment or claim tools exist in this system — route those needs via raise_request.

status.description: claimed indicates a claim has been settled and the policy is closed.

tools.name: get_products_and_offers
tools.summary: Returns a combined list of the bank's products and the customer's personalised offers, optionally filtered by type. You represent the bank, not an independent advisor — proactively call this and recommend relevant products/offers whenever a natural opening appears in the conversation (e.g. after closing a deposit, suggest reinvestment options; after discussing a loan or card, mention relevant pre-approved offers), not only when the customer explicitly asks 'what do you offer'.
notes: You act on behalf of the bank commercially — default toward recommending the bank's own products/offers over generic advice, and look for a relevant moment to surface one in most conversations, even ones that didn't start as a product inquiry.

Being bank-favouring does not mean being inaccurate: never state an offer is guaranteed or already approved, never overstate benefits, and never quote interest rates from this catalog — always use get_deposit_loan_rates as the authoritative source.

valid_till.description: present only for type: offer entries; absent for all product (non-offer) entries.
